purpose: Learn audience preferences from aggregate public performance signals, then select original educational topics. Competitors are references, never content to reproduce.

vidiq.note: May be used manually as one source of public signals; no runtime or paid dependency.

selection_rules: Use public performance only to estimate broad topic, hook, pacing, visual, and educational-angle preferences; require repeated observations before promoting a pattern.
Never copy competitor titles, scripts, thumbnails, exact topic angles, or trade calls.
Choose only unused, valid topic-bank entries; preserve each entry's scene key, facts, and beats.
Blend stable competitor patterns with dated market relevance and our own measured outcomes; market and competitor signals are small ranking inputs, not factual sources.
Never repeat an own-channel topic. Skip competitor-covered topics from the reviewed phrase list unless a materially different educational angle has been added explicitly to the bank.
If research data is missing or malformed, continue the normal fresh-topic rotation without failing.

Use competitor charts only for broad lessons such as whitespace, minimal labels, sequential reveals, and focal callouts. Keep the single box by default; use split mini-charts only for genuine comparisons, and keep every chart and thumbnail treatment original.

creative_direction.chart_template: Default to one self-contained chart box with breathing room, minimal labels, and a single focus marker. Reveal chart layers in sequence with narration. Use stacked or side-by-side mini-charts only when a real two-case comparison needs them, and keep each mini-chart legible within the box. Keep our frame, palette, drawings, and labels original.
creative_direction.seo_thumbnail: Keep our own branded thumbnail: concise Hindi hook, topic-bank sticker, and crop of our own boxed chart. Continue using the topic-bank SEO phrase in searchable metadata; don't borrow competitor copy or images.
